item.title: Carolina Science Cafe: NC’s Changing Climate — Tue Sep 1, 6:00 PM — Haw River Tap & Table
item.description:

North Carolina’s Changing Climate: Extreme Heat and Rainfall
From the mountains to the coast – North Carolina’s climate is changing. One aspect of the climate system that is of concern is the frequency, intensity, and duration of extreme heat and rainfall events. In this talk, State Climatologist & Director of the State Climate Office of NC Jared H. Bowden, PhD, will discuss observed changes in extreme heat and rainfall, the climate science that supports these changes, and provide insight into the future using climate models.
Designed for adults, Carolina Science Cafe is a free program that explores science topics making national and international headlines, offering the chance to meet the experts behind the work. This special program is hosted at Haw River Tap & Table in Carrboro on the first Tuesday of every month. Light appetizers are available for all attendees.

item.description:
The man... The myth... The legend...
NIC CAGE!
A film career that has spanned decades and genres, blockbusters and direct to video, Nic Cage is a force unto himself.
Incomparable practicing his own style of method acting which he calls Nouveau shamanism he transcends acting conventions.
The only actor meta enough to have played himself. The only actor to have become an internet meme. The only actor to have a library film discussion group devoted to him.

item.title: after work bike ride on the ATT — Tue Sep 1, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Triangle Hiking and Outdoors Group We'll be starting near Southpoint and final starting point will be sent out Monday evening.
Make sure that your bike is in good working order - tires hold air and are up to pressure, brakes and shifters work and your chain has been oiled.
We'll be riding just under 2 hours and about 22 miles. The ride is fairly flat and shaded and our pace will be moderate (about 12 mph average). I recommend a hard tail or hybrid bike, but if you really want to bring a road bike it's ok, though you'll likely be a bit bored. Unicycles....?
I'll be eating after the ride at a restaurant. You're welcome to join me if you like.
Helmets are required and by signing up you agree to THOG liability waiver statement.
Please Note!! Any cancellation less than 30 hours before the beginning of the event will be considered a "no show"

item.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (Theatre for the Very Young) — Wed Sep 2, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is an interactive children’s theatre piece for very young audiences, performed by two Star Keepers named Glimmer and Sparkle. It’s time for the night sky to fill with stars, but one important star — Little Star, the wishing star — is missing because Sparkle rushed through putting the stars away the previous morning and muddled everything up. What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place. Audience members help the Star Keepers find and re-organize the sky just in time for nightfall so that everyone can make a wish on their favorite star. Twinkle, Twinkle explores the ideas that mistakes happen, feelings are valid, and no one has to face hard things alone – all wrapped up in a genuinely joyful romp about stars.
By Ernie Nolan Produced by special arrangemen

item.title: Aging Gracefully Creative Movement Workshop — Wed Sep 2, 11:00 AM — Arts Together
item.description:
Ages 50+ Aging Gracefully: Meaningful Movement Explorations – As we age it is important to keep the body moving, the brain focused, and the spirit fueled. In this technique/creative dance class, we will do so in a healthy, FUN way. We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. Inspired by poetry, visual art, and personal experience, we will create dances; accessing the wisdom of the body to express our relationship to the world, each other, and ourselves. No prior dance experience needed, just a willing heart <3

item.title: Physics Colloquium - High Energy Physics at Low Energies: The MOLLER Experiment at Jefferson Lab — Wed Sep 2, 3:30 PM — None
item.description:
Nature violates parity symmetry. Discovered almost 70 years ago, this phenomenon implies that the universe is "left-handed." Although we have a very successful theory, the Standard Model of Particle Physics, which agrees with scores of experimental tests, includes parity violations in an ad hoc way. There are hints that the Standard Model should break down at very high energies, restoring parity symmetry. There are viable conjectures for how that might come about, and much of High Energy Physics tries to reach the energy scales where this breakdown might occur.
This talk describes a different approach, trading very high energy interactions for extremely precise measurements at lower energies. The MOLLER experiment at Jefferson Lab will measure parity violation in electron-electron scattering for which the Standard Model makes a precise prediction. Disagreement between experiment and theory at this level would indicate "new physics" at energies beyond the reach of current high energy

item.title: Enduring Hostility: The Making of America's Iran Policy — Wed Sep 2, 5:30 PM — Westbrook 0016
item.description:
Fireside chat with Dr. Dalia Dassa Kaye. Dr. Kaye is a senior fellow at the UCLA Burkle Center for International Relations and director of its Initiative on Regional Security Architectures. A life member of the Council on Foreign Relations, Dalia is an internationally recognized expert on geopolitics and Middle East policy. She is the author of dozens of articles and policy reports, as well as three books, including most recently Enduring Hostility: The Making of America's Iran Policy (Stanford University Press, 2026). This event will be recorded for archival and promotional purposes.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Chloe Moriondo — Wed Sep 2, 6:00 PM — Sarah P. Duke Gardens
item.description:
You know the feeling: something ends, everything changes, and suddenly you have to figure out who you are again. Chloe Moriondo made an album about it.
Coming to Duke as part of Arts Welcome Week, this Duke student-exclusive concert brings Moriondo's strange, shape-shifting world to campus for a night of big feelings, genre collisions, and music made for figuring things out as you go.
Written after the biggest breakup of her life, oyster transforms a period of upheaval-heartbreak, living alone for the first time, figuring out who she was outside a relationship-into a shimmering musical world. "No matter what my feelings are, they're gonna be strong. Whether I'm angry, whether I'm obsessed, whether I'm hopelessly upset, it's all going to be a lot."
The performance will open with a set from Greensboro-based indie band bedrumor.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.title: Mobile Health Assessment — Thu Sep 3, 9:30 AM — None
item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Additionally, there is a goal setting and referral session with a nurse, dietitian, or fitness specialist. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.

item.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (Theatre for the Very Young) — Sat Sep 5, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is an interactive children’s theatre piece for very young audiences, performed by two Star Keepers named Glimmer and Sparkle. It’s time for the night sky to fill with stars, but one important star — Little Star, the wishing star — is missing because Sparkle rushed through putting the stars away the previous morning and muddled everything up. What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place. Audience members help the Star Keepers find and re-organize the sky just in time for nightfall so that everyone can make a wish on their favorite star. Twinkle, Twinkle explores the ideas that mistakes happen, feelings are valid, and no one has to face hard things alone – all wrapped up in a genuinely joyful romp about stars.
By Ernie Nolan Produced by special arrangemen

item.title: Lectures in Art History: Art, Health, and Equity series featuring Tanya Sheehan, Colby College — Mon Sep 14, 5:30 PM — Chapman Hall
item.description:
Department of Art and Art History
“Communities of Care: Charles Alston, Jacob Lawrence, and the Murals of Harlem Hospital”
When Jacob Lawrence first painted an image of Harlem Hospital in 1937, Harlem’s largest public healthcare facility was teamed with artists hired by the federal government and working under the supervision of Lawrence’s art teacher and mentor, Charles Alston. Although the young painter was not officially assigned to Alston’s team, significant connections to the murals can be found in his artwork, in the murals themselves, and in their shared participation in a discourse on race, medicine, and health in urban America. In exploring these connections, this talk shows how Black life could and could not be represented on the walls of Harlem Hospital, and how a commitment to care within and for Black communities took shape in Lawrence’s art.
Tanya Sheehan is James M. Gillespie Professor and Chair of the Department of Science, Technology, and Society at Colby

item.title: Migrating Monarchs — Thu Sep 17, 10:00 AM — Prairie Ridge
item.description:
All programs at Prairie Ridge currently require registration. Register Join us for a front-row seat to one of nature’s most incredible journeys, the Monarch butterfly migration! We’ll start this family friendly program in our Nature Neighborhood Garden to explore the habitats we steward here at Prairie Ridge and see how these spaces fuel Monarchs along their trek south. Then, we’ll head into the prairie to spot as many butterflies as we can! If we’re lucky, we might even catch and release a live Monarch butterfly. We will learn about the Monarch Larvae Monitoring Project and Monarch Watch collaborative science projects along the way.
